jobs.title: Equipment Management and Environmental Monitoring Manager
jobs.description:
Overview

Element Concord has a current opening for an Equipment Manager/Environmental Monitoring Manager
to join our growing team. The Equipment Management/Environmental Monitoring Manager
is responsible for leading Element Concord’s Cleanroom Services, Equipment Management programs, and client Environmental Monitoring (EM) services. This role oversees department operations, personnel training and development, technical execution, client communication, and compliance with applicable quality, client, and regulatory requirements. The position ensures services are performed safely, accurately, on time, and in accordance with established procedures and standards, including ISO/IEC 17025, USP, GMP, FDA, and ICH guidelines.

$90k-$110k DOE

Responsibilities

LEADERSHIP AND DEPARTMENT MANAGEMENT

Provide day-to-day leadership, direction, coaching, and oversight for Environmental Monitoring personnel
Manage equipment lifecycle activities in support of equipment calibration, validation, and PM activities
Support personnel training, qualifications, mentoring, workload planning, and development to ensure assigned duties are performed competently and consistently
Promote a culture of safety, quality, accountability, continuous improvement, and compliance with Element policies and procedures
Ensure departmental activities are prioritized and completed in alignment with client commitments, internal timelines, and business needs

EQUIPMENT MANAGEMENT

Oversee equipment management activities, including qualification support, calibration, preventive maintenance, repair coordination, and equipment status tracking
Ensure equipment used for laboratory and cleanroom operations remains appropriately maintained, documented, and suitable for use
Coordinate vendor services and internal stakeholders to support timely completion of equipment-related activities
Support equipment-related investigations, change controls, risk assessments, and continuous improvement initiatives

ENVIRONMENTAL MONITORING AND CLEANROOM SERVICES

Manage Environmental Monitoring services and cleanroom-related activities to ensure sampling, testing, and documentation are performed in accordance with approved procedures and client requirements
Ensure monitoring and laboratory activities are performed in compliance with applicable quality system, regulatory, and data integrity expectations
Oversee preparation, review, and execution of protocols, procedures, forms, and reports associated with Environmental Monitoring and cleanroom operations
Review Environmental Monitoring data, trends, deviations, and excursions and support timely investigation, corrective action, and effectiveness activities as applicable
Support cleanroom qualification, requalification, contamination control, and operational readiness activities as required

QUALITY, COMPLIANCE, AND DOCUMENTATION

Ensure department activities comply with the Quality Manual, applicable SOPs, client requirements, and relevant regulatory expectations
Maintain documentation practices consistent with Good Documentation Practices (GDP) and data integrity requirements
Support internal audits, client audits, regulatory inspections, and quality system assessments within the department’s scope
Review and support SOPs, protocols, reports, deviations, CAPAs, and change controls associated with Environmental Monitoring, cleanroom services, and equipment management

CLIENT COMMUNICATION AND BUSINESS PERFORMANCE

Communicate professionally with clients to discuss project requirements, resolve issues, support customer satisfaction, and maintain strong business relationships
Ensure efficient departmental operations and support achievement of revenue, EBITDA, productivity, and service delivery objectives
Identify and implement process improvements that strengthen compliance, efficiency, turnaround time, and customer experience

Required Qualifications

Skills / Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree or higher in Microbiology, Engineering, Biology, Life Sciences, or a related scientific discipline
Minimum of two years of experience, preferably in a GMP-regulated laboratory or related controlled environment
Hands-on knowledge of Environmental Monitoring programs and cleanroom operations
Working knowledge of applicable standards and regulatory expectations, including ISO/IEC 17025, USP, GMP, FDA, and ICH guidelines
Strong organizational, written communication, verbal communication, problem-solving, and prioritization skills
Ability to lead personnel, coordinate cross-functional activities, and manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced laboratory environment
Prior supervisory or management experience in a laboratory, cleanroom, pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or contract testing environment
Experience with equipment lifecycle management, calibration programs, preventive maintenance systems, investigations, CAPAs, and change control processes
Experience supporting client audits, regulatory inspections, or quality system assessments

Physical And Work Environment Requirements

Ability to work in laboratory and controlled cleanroom environments as required
Ability to wear required personal protective equipment (PPE)
Ability to stand, walk, and move between laboratory, cleanroom, and office areas as business needs require
Other duties may be assigned as needed

Company Overview

Element is one of the fastest growing testing, inspection and certification businesses in the world. Globally we have more than 9,000 brilliant minds operating from 270 sites across 30 countries. Together we share an ambitious purpose to ‘Make tomorrow safer than today’.

When failure in use is not an option, we help customers make certain that their products, materials, processes and services are safe, compliant and fit for purpose. From early R&D, through complex regulatory approvals and into production, our global laboratory network of scientists, engineers, and technologists support customers to achieve assurance over product quality, sustainable outcomes, and market access.

While we are proud of our global reach, working at Element feels like being part of a smaller company. We empower you to take charge of your career, and reward excellence and integrity with growth and development.

Industries across the world depend on our care, attention to detail and the absolute accuracy of our work. The role we have to play in creating a safer world is much bigger than our organization.

Diversity Statement

At Element, we always take pride in putting our people first. We are an equal opportunity employer that recognizes diversity and inclusion as fundamental to our Vision of becoming “the world’s most trusted testing partner”.

All suitably qualified candidates will receive consideration for employment on the basis of objective work related criteria and without regard for the following: age, disability, ethnic origin, gender, marital status, race, religion, responsibility of dependents, sexual orientation, or gender identity or other characteristics in accordance with the applicable governing laws or other characteristics in accordance with the applicable governing laws.

The contractor will not discharge or in any other manner discriminate against employees or applicants because they have inquired about, discussed, or disclosed their own pay or the pay of another employee or applicant. However, employees who have access to the compensation information of other employees or applicants as a part of their essential job functions cannot disclose the pay of other employees or applicants to individuals who do not otherwise have access to compensation information, unless the disclosure is (a) in response to a formal complaint or charge, (b) in furtherance of an investigation, proceeding, hearing, or action, including an investigation conducted by the employer, or (c) consistent with the contractor’s legal duty to furnish information. 41 CFR 60-1.35(c)

jobs.title: Manager, Environmental Compliance & Strategy
jobs.description:
Company Overview

Pattern Energy is a leading renewable energy company that develops, constructs, owns, and operates high-quality wind and solar generation, transmission, and energy storage facilities. Our mission is to transition the world to renewable energy through the sustainable development and responsible operation of facilities with respect for the environment, communities, and cultures where we have a presence.

Our approach begins and ends with establishing trust, accountability, and transparency. Our company values of creative spirit, pride of ownership, follow-through, and a team-first attitude drive us to pursue our mission every day. Our culture supports our values by fostering innovative and critical thinking and a deep belief in living up to our promises.

Pattern Energy operates in the United States and Canada, with offices in San Francisco, Houston, San Diego, New York and Toronto. Pattern Energy Group's corporate headquarters are in San Francisco. Pattern has a global portfolio of more than 35 power facilities and transmission assets, serving various customers that provide low-cost clean energy to millions of consumers.

Responsibilities

JOB PURPOSE

The Manager, Environmental Compliance & Strategy, EPC is responsible for ensuring environmental compliance and supporting strategic risk planning for Pattern’s projects during execution, with a primary focus on wind, transmission, and solar energy projects in the United States and Canada, and ancillary support for compliance efforts in other jurisdictions as needed.

This role leads and coordinates environmental construction permit compliance activities, supports environmental compliance programs and tools, and works closely with internal project teams, consultants, contractors, regulatory authorities, and local interest groups to ensure Pattern’s projects meet applicable environmental permit, regulatory, and internal compliance requirements.

To support ongoing Pattern projects, viable candidates may also be considered if they live near Pattern project locations in Arizona, Arkansas, Colorado, Louisiana, Montana, North Dakota, or New Mexico, as an optional work location arrangement.

Key Accountabilities

The key responsibilities will include as a minimum the following:

Lead environmental construction permit compliance activities in coordination with Pattern EPC group managers, engineering and construction managers, project construction contractors, and Pattern Environmental Development and Operations teams.
Manage and coordinate project environmental personnel, including environmental consultants, EPC and specialty contractors, regulatory authorities, and local interest groups as appropriate.
Conduct environmental compliance reviews, participate in monthly management meetings, complete site audits, and support compliance root-cause analysis investigations and reviews.
Assist in the development and implementation of Pattern environmental compliance programs, procedures, and project execution documents.
Create, maintain, and update project environmental compliance matrices during project execution.
Develop and deliver Environmental Awareness Training for EPC and contractor staff.
Coordinate with federal, state, provincial, and local environmental agency leads to resolve environmental concerns during construction.
Budget for and manage consultants providing project-level environmental support services, including construction environmental monitoring and wildlife mitigation strategies.
Represent Pattern in industry organizations and technical committees, supporting benchmarking, collaboration, and thought leadership across the renewable energy sector.

Qualifications

Experience/Qualifications/Education Required

Educational Experience

A bachelor’s degree in a science-oriented field such as Biology, Ecology, Environmental Sciences, Wildlife, or a related field is required. An advanced degree in Law, Biology, Environmental Sciences, Ecology, or a comparable discipline is preferred.

Required Work Experience

The following criteria will be used as a basis for Pattern to select a qualified applicant:

Seven or more years of experience in environmental, natural resources, or energy-related projects, preferably in renewable energy.
Experience with wind, transmission, and/or solar power permitting, environmental construction compliance, and environmental fieldwork.
Familiarity with federal, state, and provincial environmental regulations related to stormwater, hazardous materials, hazardous waste, air quality, wildlife, archaeology, environmental due diligence, and associated compliance programs.
Extensive experience with stormwater best management practices, including design, implementation, maintenance, and cost considerations.
Experience collaborating with cross-functional project teams and managing environmental consultants and contractors.

Additional Requirements

Must possess strengths in the following:

Strong time management, diplomacy, and specialized environmental compliance knowledge.
Ability to make informed recommendations regarding the interpretation and application of environmental permits, regulations, and laws in evolving regulatory environments.
Ability to analyze, organize, and interpret data from multiple sources and translate findings into clear written deliverables.
Strong professional communication skills, including the ability to influence best practices and change within projects and the broader organization.
Ability to multi-task, adapt quickly, work well under pressure, collaborate in large teams and one-on-one settings, and work independently with minimal supervision.
Willingness and ability to travel as needed, up to approximately 25%, depending on project needs.

Technical Skills

Computer skills – working knowledge of Windows-based business software applications, including Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook, and PowerPoint.

Environmental compliance – detailed knowledge of environmental regulatory frameworks, including wildlife, natural resources, stormwater, site restoration, spills, waste, audits, and project-specific permit or regulatory requirements for projects in the United States and/or Canada.

The expected starting pay range for this role is $103,000 - $138,000 USD. This range is an estimate and base pay may be above or below the ranges based on several factors including but not limited to location, work experience, certifications, and education. In addition to base pay, Pattern’s compensation program includes a bonus structure for full-time employees of all levels. We also provide a comprehensive benefits package which includes medical, dental, vision, short and long-term disability, life insurance, voluntary benefits, family care benefits, employee assistance program, paid time off and bonding leave, paid holidays, 401(k)/RRSP retirement savings plan with employer contribution, and employee referral bonuses.

Pattern Energy Group LP is an equal opportunity employer

jobs.title: Environmental Health Safety Specialist
jobs.description:
JOB RESPONSIBILITIES
Have oversight of Industrial Hygiene, Fire Prevention LOTO, PPE, etc. Ensure that programs are in place to assist in meeting Company objectives.
Ensure training programs and in place to ensure compliance.
Implement accident, near miss, and observation reporting programs to proactively manage safety performance.
Lead root cause analysis investigation and manage documentation confirm corrective actions have been put in place ensuring complete case management of injuries (reporting, workers compensation, return to work, etc.).
Build communications required to present incident details and corrective action plans to diffident levels of the business.
Ensure Job Safety and Environmental Analyses/Job Hazard Analysis are being conducted as required.
Evaluate operational practices to determine methods to eliminate workplace hazards.
Environmental knowledge of applicable federal, state, and local regulations.
Willingness and interest in learning about environmental regulations (air, water & waste) permitting, compliance and recordkeeping requirements.
Assist with EHS audits and training programs as needed.
Establish a working relationship with appropriate regulatory agency personnel.

QUALIFICATIONS
Bachelor’s degree in Health & Safety or the Sciences
Min of 3+ years of Health & Safety experience 2 years in a manufacturing environment.
Experience with OSHA, LOTO, Root Cause Analysis
Union experience a plus
Needs to have occasional flexibility on start time.

jobs.description:
Job Description

Manages the ongoing preparation, testing, and monitoring of compliance with information security standards and government regulations and regulatory agencies as it relates to the design, development, and deployment of products and services.

Responsibilities

The Director, Risk Management and Regulatory Compliance, will coordinate closely with operations teams which may include Global Business Units, Corporate Security, and with Oracle Legal. Responsibilities include developing and maintaining comprehensive information security, and/or quality management, and regulatory oversight program, including standards for product and service design aligned with Oracle Software Security Assurance and Security Architecture Review, and/or quality management system standards. Will be responsible for managing information security risks and managing compliance team. Will educate through training members on information security and industry regulatory standards applicable to their products and services. Work with respective teams which may include GBU development, operations, and service, to incorporate applicable industry regulatory standards, Oracle security and/or quality policies and customer-contractual obligations into processes and standards. Work with Corporate Security and Business Assessment and Audit, and/or Quality System Internal Audit to evaluate product and service line security and regulatory compliance on an ongoing basis. Work with Legal to evaluate changes in applicable laws and regulations and impact on products and services. Work with Corporate Development and Legal to evaluate potential acquisitions for regulatory issues. Administrate industry and regulatory certifications, including managing certification vendors (e.g., PCI, HIPAA, HITECH, ISO).

Qualifications

Career Level - M4

About Us

Only Oracle brings together the data, infrastructure, applications, and expertise to power everything from industry innovations to life-saving care. And with AI embedded across our products and services, we help customers turn that promise into a better future for all. Discover your potential at a company leading the way in AI and cloud solutions that impact billions of lives.

True innovation starts when everyone is empowered to contribute. That’s why we’re committed to growing a workforce that promotes opportunities for all with competitive benefits that support our people with flexible medical, life insurance, and retirement options. We also encourage employees to give back to their communities through our volunteer programs.

We’re committed to including people with disabilities at all stages of the employment process. If you require accessibility assistance or accommodation for a disability at any point, let us know by emailing accommodation-request_mb@oracle.com or by calling 1-888-404-2494 in the United States.

Oracle is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability and protected veterans’ status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Oracle will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records pursuant to applicable law.
